name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Automate prompt review with PR-Agent.

PR-Agent already reviews pull requests for quality—it’s free, open-source, and proven. Hook it into our prompt/engine/routing codebase to scan every change for prompt drift, unsafe routing, or code smells. It catches issues humans miss and does it at scale.

Trade-off: False positives. PR-Agent isn’t perfect—it might flag harmless tweaks as risky. Accept that noise; we’ll tune thresholds and keep human review for edge cases. The alternative—manual review—slows us down and misses subtle bugs.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent optimizes for *code* reviews, not *prompt* drift—its static analysis won’t catch semantic shifts in instructions or routing logic until runtime. A better alternative: embed a lightweight prompt validator in our engine that flags changes to system prompts or routing rules *before* they hit PR-Agent, then let PR-Agent handle the code. Settle it by running a controlled test: measure how many prompt-related issues PR-Agent misses versus the validator catches in a week of real changes.
